title: The challenge of synthesis dependence in quantum materials research
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 01 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03417-x

Interesting results in quantum materials often suffer from substantial inconsistencies between samples. This Perspective advocates for more careful study of synthesis dependence to realize the full potential of quantum materials science.

title: Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 31 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03429-7

Driving a solid with light can create a topological insulator, but controlling its electrons has remained elusive. Optical control of electrons in a Floquet topological insulator has now been achieved in light-dressed graphene.

title: Electric-field control of coherent ferron oscillations
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 27 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03406-0

Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of ferrons—collective excitations of electric polarization—is crucial for device applications. Now electric-field control of coherent ferron oscillations is demonstrated in a layered ferroelectric.

title: Sound protection for electron spins
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 24 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03365-6

Solid state electron spins have important practical advantages for quantum technologies, but fluctuations in their host material cause decoherence. Now, it has been shown that sound waves can extend the coherence of diamond silicon vacancy spins.

title: Real-space imaging of moiré-confined excitons in twisted bilayer MoS<sub>2</sub>
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 24 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03425-x

Moiré excitons have been widely observed in twisted two-dimensional semiconductors but have not been directly imaged at room temperature. Now, this is achieved using photocurrent atomic force microscopy.

title: Decaying and expanding Erk gradients process memory of skeletal size during zebrafish fin regeneration
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 24 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03426-w

Zebrafish can regenerate amputated fins back to their original size. It is now shown that gradients in extracellular signal-regulated kinase activity act as rulers during fin bone regeneration.

title: Electrons surf farther on plasma waves
abstract:
Nature Physics, Published online: 21 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03410-4

The energy gain of laser wakefield accelerators is tied to the distance over which electrons are accelerated. Now this limitation can be overcome with flying-focus laser pulses, allowing electrons to surf the plasma wave over longer distances.
